origin.description: Equi-tailed two-sided approximate bootstrap confidence intervals from numerical derivatives of a statistic.
origin.usage:
abc.ci(data, statistic, index = 1, strata = rep(1, n), conf = 0.95,
       eps = 0.001/n, ...)

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: A vector, matrix, or data frame. One row is one observation.

arguments.name: statistic
arguments.text: Function of the data and a weight vector. The weights are normalized to sum to 1 inside each stratum. Further arguments are passed through unchanged.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based position of the component of interest when the statistic returns several numbers. Only the first position is used.

arguments.name: strata
arguments.text: Stratum label for each observation. The default is one sample. The default and the default of eps are evaluated after n is known.

arguments.name: eps
arguments.text: Step for the numerical derivatives. The default is 0.001/n.
Further arguments passed to statistic on every call.

origin.details: The calculation follows abcnon as given by DiCiccio and Efron. Finite differences supply the influence values and the second derivatives. Those constants approximate the BCa endpoints. The statistic is evaluated 2*n + 2 + 2*length(conf) times, plus once at the original weights. Stratum weights are normalized inside the function, so the statistic does not have to be rewritten for several samples. The two tails of each level are interleaved, lower then upper, rather than all lower endpoints first. The manual describes a matrix for every conf. The installed function returns a length-3 vector when conf has length 1.
origin.value: When conf has length 1, a vector of length 3: the level and the two endpoints. Otherwise a matrix with one row per level and those three columns.
origin.example:
library(boot)
mean_w <- function(d, w) sum(d * w)
print(abc.ci(1:8, mean_w, conf = c(0.90, 0.95)))

translation.description: Equi-tailed two-sided approximate bootstrap confidence intervals from numerical derivatives of a statistic.
translation.usage: abc_ci(data, statistic, index=1, strata=None, conf=0.95, eps=None, **kwargs)

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: A one-dimensional array, or a two-dimensional array with one row per observation.

arguments.name: statistic
arguments.text: Function of the data and a weight vector. The weights are normalized to sum to 1 inside each stratum. Further keyword arguments are passed through unchanged.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based position of the component of interest. If several positions are given, only the first is used, with a warning.

arguments.name: strata
arguments.text: Stratum label for each observation. None is one sample. Labels are renumbered as R renumbers them: sorted unique numbers become 1, 2, and so on.

arguments.name: eps
arguments.text: Step for the numerical derivatives. None means 0.001/n, with n taken from the data.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Further arguments passed to statistic on every call.

translation.details: Finite differences supply the influence values and the second derivatives, and those constants approximate the BCa endpoints. The statistic is evaluated 2*n + 2 + 2*length(conf) times, plus once at the original weights. The two tails of each level are interleaved, lower then upper. One confidence level is a length-3 vector. Several levels are a matrix. The calculation does not draw random numbers.
translation.value: A length-3 NumPy array when conf has one level. Otherwise an array with one row per level and three columns: the level and the two endpoints.
